paraphrase: Mind is said to be of two kinds, pure and impure: impure when joined with desire, pure when free of desire.

paraphrase: There is no dissolution, no origination, no one bound, no seeker, no aspirant for liberation and none liberated — this is the highest truth.

checks.note: E-text 10 located; the passage matches the paraphrase (it begins: 'na nirodho nacotpattirna vandyo na ca śāsanam | na mumukṣā na muktiścedityeṣā paramārthatā|| 10…').

paraphrase: The one Self abides in waking, dream and deep sleep; the one being-self appears many in beings like the moon in water; as space in a pot is not destroyed when the pot breaks, the Self is not destroyed with the body.

checks.note: E-text 11-13 located; the passage matches the paraphrase (it begins: '2 || eka evātmā mantavyo jāgratsvapnasuṣuptiṣu | sthānatrayādvyatī-tasya punarjanma na vidyate || 11 || eka…').

paraphrase: Two Brahmans are to be known, the word-Brahman and the supreme; one versed in the word-Brahman reaches the supreme. Having studied the books, the wise one devoted to knowledge should cast them away like husk after taking the grain.

checks.note: E-text 16-18 located; the passage matches the paraphrase (it begins: '3 || śabdākṣaraṃ paraṃ brahma yasminkṣīṇe yadakṣa-ram | tadvidvānakṣaraṃ dhyāyedyadīcchecchāntimātmanaḥ || 16…').

paraphrase: Mind alone is the cause of human bondage and liberation: attached to objects it leads to bondage, free of objects to liberation.

paraphrase: Knowledge is hidden in every being like ghee in milk; it is to be churned with the mind as churning rod. The knower concludes: 'I am Vāsudeva', the partless, stainless Brahman in whom all beings dwell.

paraphrase: When the mind, free of attachment and restrained in the heart, becomes non-existent (unmanībhāva), that is the supreme state; it should be restrained until it perishes in the heart — this is knowledge and meditation, the rest is extension of books.
